title: Staged dependency graph & graceful operator rollback acceptance criteria for Private/VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
Many Private/VPC customers require deterministic upgrades and artifact provisioning with either no egress or tightly controlled egress. Engineering has delivered offline bundle sync and mirror support, but we lack a formalized 'staged dependency graph' spec (what artifact groups to fetch and when) and a documented, testable operator rollback contract for partial failures during upgrades. This ticket captures product requirements and acceptance criteria for both: (1) a minimal staged dependency graph for bootstrapping/upgrades that minimizes egress and (2) a graceful operator rollback and recovery contract when an upgrade step fails in limited-egress environments.

Goals:
- Define the staged dependency graph: ordering, chunking, and backoff semantics for artifact fetches under restricted egress and mirror-only modes.
- Define deterministic validation checks (checksum, signed manifest provenance, timestamp tolerance) that must pass before advancing stages.
- Define an operator rollback contract: safe quiesce API, snapshot points, time-bounded rollback window, and observable state transitions for customers and SRE.
- Provide acceptance tests and harnesses that can run in a simulated air-gapped environment (local mirror + network partition tests).

Scope (in):
- Bootstrap and upgrade flows for Private operator and node agents.
- Manifest signing + checksum verification and mirror token rotation semantics.
- MTU-aware streaming for large artifacts and retry/backoff behavior.
- Canary simulation harness that can inject partial mirror failures and validate rollback.

Out of scope:
- New operator feature work unrelated to upgrade/rollback (e.g., new CRD functionality).
- Multi-region geo-replication for mirrors (follow-up).

Acceptance criteria (must all be met):
1) Staged dependency graph spec accepted: document that lists stage order (control-plane binaries, operator CRDs, sidecars, images, bootstrapping bundles), maximum stage size (bytes) for streaming, and per-stage network policy requirements.
2) Deterministic validation: every stage must implement manifest signature validation and SHA256 checksum verification. If validation fails, stage must not advance and must emit a specific audit log entry including manifest id and failure reason.
3) No-egress/mirror-only success path: a private deploy configured with a customer mirror (with optional authentication token) successfully completes a full operator upgrade using only the mirror. The run must be reproducible in our CI airgap harness (see test link).
4) Graceful rollback contract: operator exposes a /quiesce API that halts new work and creates a recovery snapshot. If post-stage health checks fail for > N minutes (configurable, default 10m), operator will automatically revert to previous snapshot within a bounded window and mark the cluster 'upgrade-failed' with remediation hints.
5) Rollback observability: all state transitions (started-stage, validated-stage, applied-stage, rollback-initiated, rollback-complete) are emitted as structured audit events and visible in Console telemetry (per-route model for private).
6) Telemetry & alerts: defined SLOs for upgrade success rate (> 99% in CI sim), and automated alerting when rollback occurs. Alert runbook must reference the operator rollback runbook and mirror health dashboard.
7) Test matrix: automated tests covering (a) successful mirror-only upgrade, (b) manifest checksum failure mid-stage -> stop and alert, (c) partial mirror IO timeout causing rollback, (d) MTU fragmentation causing chunked retry recovery. Test artifacts include GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/412 and Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Private+Staged+Dependencies.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement spec + unit tests; run CI airgap harness against 3 internal mirror configurations.
- Phase 2 (partner validation): invite two customers (one regulated, one infra-heavy) to run canary with support; collect telemetry and adjust timeouts.
- Phase 3 (GA): enable staged dependency graph as opt-in flag in private operator; default to 'conservative' staging.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default rollback window: should we set 10m or 30m for first GA? (engineering preference: 10m; ops preference: 30m).
- Manifest provenance: require KMS-signed manifests or accept ephemeral repository signatures?

Links / artifacts:
- Airgap harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/airgap-harness (test-cases/upgrade-sim).
- Design notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-private-staged-dependencies-design.
- Related tickets: PM-42069 (private network verification), ENG-1842 (operator snapshot API).

Decision log & next steps:
- PM to align on default rollback window by 2026-02-05.
- Engineering to deliver prototype manifest verifier and /quiesce endpoint in branch 'staged-upgrades/prototype' and open PR against private-operator.
- Schedule partner validation with Customer Success for 2026-03-20.
